events.text: Delta Says Government Shutdown Dented Profit by $200 Million
events.context:
Delta Says Government Shutdown Dented Profit by $200 Million
Delta Air Lines said it expects this fall’s U.S. government shutdown to erode its fourth-quarter profit by about $200 million. The carrier said Wednesday that the 43-day shutdown, which spurred regulators to curb air traffic at 40 major airports last month, would dent its earnings by about 25 cents a share. Bookings fell by 5% to 10% during the 10 days that flight restrictions were in effect, with business travel softening and refunds surging, Delta Chief Executive Ed Bastian said Wednesday at a conference.

events.context:
Delta Air Lines (DAL) Premium Demand and Pricing Power Support Growth Despite Fuel Risks
Delta Air Lines Inc.'s (NYSE:DAL) results exceeded management's guidance for the June quarter. Premium products and diversified, high-margin revenue streams accounted for 61% of the company's adjusted operating revenue. Premium revenue increased 17% year-over-year, amid continued investments in premium seating and strengthened yields. The company posted adjusted EPS of $1.56 along with $1.7 billion in adjusted operating cash flows. Based on recent quarter outcomes, management upheld its full-year FY26 guidance with 20% growth projection for earnings. events.text: Quicker Boeing deliveries help Ryanair boost profit, traffic forecast
events.context:
Quicker Boeing deliveries help Ryanair boost profit, traffic forecast
STORY: Ryanair profits flew up 42% in the first six months of the year.The budget airline reported a forecast-beating $2.96 billion on Monday (November 3).That was well up from the same period last year and above analyst projections.Average fares also grew by 13% year-on-year.Ryanair also raised its passenger traffic forecast Monday.It cited earlier than expected Boeing deliveries and strong first-half demand.The carrier said it cautiously expects to recover all of last year's 7% average fare decline in the financial year to March end.It further added this should lead to what it called 'reasonable' full-year net profit growth.Ryanair expects to fly 207 million passengers to end-March - up by a million from a previous forecast.The uptick comes after the airline received 23 new MAX 8 aircraft from Boeing.Ryanair said it is confident of receiving the six remaining MAX 8 aircraft from an order that had suffered long delays by February.Shares were down over 2% in early Monday trade.

events.text: Ryanair flags weakness in summer fares, but risk of fuel shortage recedes
events.context:
Ryanair flags weakness in summer fares, but risk of fuel shortage recedes
STORY: Ryanair warned on Monday of weakness in ticket prices during its peak summer months.But the budget airline also said the threat of fuel shortages was falling back.It cited suppliers adapting to the ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz.The carrier said last week it didn't expect disruption to jet fuel supplies in Europe this summer.Though it cautioned its profit might come under some pressure if oil prices stayed high for longer.The airline also said it's now "increasingly confident" there won't be disruption to jet fuel supplies even after the summer.But earlier forecasts of a low-single-digit-percentage increase in fares during the peak summer months have fallen away.Ryanair said pricing fell by a mid-single-digit percentage in the April-June quarter.And it was "trending broadly flat" for the July-to-September period.The comments came as Ryanair reported a record profit for the fiscal year that ended in March.It saw an after-tax profit of $2.63 billion for the fiscal year - just ahead of analyst projections.Ryanair shares were down 3% after Monday's update.

company.description: Spirax Group plc provides thermal energy and fluid technology solutions in Europe, the Middle East, Africa, the Asia Pacific, and the Americas. It operates through three segments: Steam Thermal Solutions, Electric Thermal Solutions, and Watson-Marlow Fluid Technology Solutions. The company offers industrial and commercial steam systems, including condensate management, controls, and thermal energy management products and solutions for heating, curing, cooking, drying, cleaning, sterilizing, space heating, humidifying, vacuum packing, and producing hot water; electrical process heating and temperature management solutions, such as industrial heaters and systems, heat tracing, and various component technologies; and designs and manufactures peristaltic and niche pumps and associated fluid path technologies, including tubing, specialised filling systems and products for single use applications. The company serves food and beverage, pharmaceutical and biotechnology, oil and gas, chemical, power generation, healthcare, buildings, water and wastewater, semiconductor, transport, original equipment manufacturers machinery, and mining and precious metal processing industries. The company was formerly known as Spirax-Sarco Engineering plc and changed its name to Spirax Group PLC in June 2024. Spirax Group PLC was founded in 1888 and is headquartered in Cheltenham, the United Kingdom.
